Logos in the Wild: Pebble Beach 🌲

There’s a reason this one is instantly recognizable.

The Lone Cypress is unmistakably Pebble Beach, but what really stands out is how well the mark works everywhere. On a golf ball, a hat, a cart, a bag, signage. Big or small, full lockup or just the tree, you know exactly what you’re looking at.

That kind of versatility is part of what makes a great golf logo last.

Logos have become the most talked-about—and least explored—element of modern golf. Thus the new book, “The Best Logos in Golf” by LINKS Editor George Peper, which tallies the top 100.

Winged Foot Golf Club is a spinoff of the New York Athletic Club, founded in 1868 with the goal of bringing “structure to the nascent world of amateur sport.” The club’s symbol was a bare foot appended with a white wing, the creation of club member W. Henry Ficken, a national champion hurdler and high jumper who also happened to be a prominent architect. His design, symbolizing speed, agility, and freedom, originated with the winged sandals of Hermes, the Greek messenger of the gods.

Members of the NYAC had interest in a broad range of sports from track and field to boxing, and they soon began forming their own sub-clubs. The burgeoning golf contingent hoped to purchase land and build a course under the NYAC banner, but that idea was turned down by the club powers, so the golfers went out on their own. Winged Foot’s pioneers took the club logo with them, changing it only slightly with the addition of a crossed driver and iron in the background, and that design has remained in place for more than a century.
